step1_analysis.description: A high-speed photoreceiver front-end consisting of a common-source TIA core with a source-follower and feedback resistor, followed by a cascode output buffer to drive the load.

paper_reference.title: Photoreceiver Module Using an InP HEMT Transimpedance Amplifier for Over 40 Gb/s

Transimpedance Gain (Zt).description: Ratio of output voltage to input current, representing the conversion gain of the TIA.

sky130_expected.calculation: Zt ≈ Rf * Gain_buffer. With Rf=1kΩ and a cascode buffer gain of ~0.6 V/V, Zt ≈ 600 Ω. In dBΩ, 20*log10(600) ≈ 55 dBΩ.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 has lower mobility and transconductance compared to InP HEMT, resulting in lower open-loop gain and buffer gain.

Bandwidth.description: -3dB cutoff frequency of the transimpedance gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: Dominated by the input pole: 1 / (2*π*Cin*Rin). Assuming Cin=50fF (PD capacitance) and Rin ≈ Rf/A ≈ 200Ω, BW ≈ 16 GHz. However, device fT and parasitic capacitances will limit this further.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 130nm CMOS is significantly slower than the ultrahigh-speed InP HEMT technology used in the paper, drastically reducing the achievable bandwidth.

Power Consumption.description: Total DC power dissipated by the circuit.

sky130_expected.reasoning: A CMOS implementation at 1.8V consumes much less power than the high-current, high-speed InP HEMT implementation.

Output Voltage Swing.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage for a given input current swing.

sky130_expected.calculation: For a 10µA peak input current and Zt=600Ω, Vout_peak = 10µA * 600Ω = 6mV. Vout_pp = 12mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends directly on the input current amplitude and the transimpedance gain.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure transimpedance gain, bandwidth, power consumption, and output swing of the TIA.
step3_testbench.spice:
* TIA Testbench
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* DUT Parameters
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

* DUT Netlist
XM1 N1 IN GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N2 N1 N3 N3 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM5 OUT N9 N10 N10 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N10 N6 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Biasing and Loads
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
R1 VDD N1 1k
V_N2 VDD N2 0
R2 N3 0 1k
RF N3 IN 1k
C_PD IN 0 50f
V_N9 N9 0 1.2
V_N6 N3 N6 0
R3 VDD OUT 500

* Input Source (AC=1 for Zt in dB, Tran=10uA sine)
IIN 0 IN DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 10u 100MEG)

.control
* DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD)*1.8
print power

* AC Analysis for Transimpedance Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 100 1MEG 100G
let zt_db = vdb(out)
meas ac zt_max max zt_db
meas ac bw_3db when zt_db='zt_max-3' fall=1

* Transient Analysis for Output Swing
tran 10p 20n
meas tran vout_pp pp v(out)

quit
.endc
.end
